newsitem.title: CROATIA: UN salutes Belgian soldier killed in Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: UN salutes Belgian soldier killed in Bosnia.

text.p: U.N. peacekeepers in Croatia's last rebel Serb enclave held a commemorative service on Sunday for a Belgian soldier killed there last week.
Corporal Olivier Gossye died on Friday when a young Serb, now in U.N. custody, opened fire on the soldier's car.
Gossye's remains were to be flown to Belgium later on Sunday from a local airport at Klisa, near Osijek in Eastern Slavonia, a U.N. spokesman told reporters.
A member of a 5,000-strong international force supporting the U.N. Transitional Administration of Eastern Slavonia (UNTAES), Gossye was the first U.N. casualty in the region.
A Jordanian soldier and an UNTAES civilian officer from the Ivory Coast were wounded in the attack.
The Croatian government blamed the incident on local Serb leaders reluctant to accept the region's reintegration into Croatia.
The U.N. secretary-general and the United States condemned the killing, but it was reported to be an isolated criminal act rather than politically motivated.
On Friday, the U.N. Security Council gave Croatia the green light to hold local elections in Eastern Slavonia in March.
